title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a preregistered, fully archived, verifier‑grounded paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) that compared a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM generator (declared_model_version = gpt‑5‑mini) on N = 120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks. The design used shared canonical candidate semantics for the confirmatory seed (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate"). All confirmatory validator episodes completed: baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt‑5‑mini, seed_0) = 120/120 verifier passes. Paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.0. We present the exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes required to reproduce the run, analyze why the paired outcome is degenerate (shared‑candidate confirmatory semantics, templated task synthesis, and validator–task coupling), and give artifact‑grounded recommendations (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed sensitivity, validator diversity, task heterogeneity) for informative follow‑ups. All execution, scoring, and analysis artifacts (execution/*, analysis/*) and a full hash manifest are released for audit; representative artifacts and hashes are cited inline.

sections.introduction: Automating network operations (NetOps) by mapping human intent to device configuration is an active research and operational domain. Generative LLMs promise natural‑language driven provisioning, but operational correctness (reachability, ACL equivalence, policy preservation, ordering and transient safety) is safety‑critical. Prior engineering and research emphasize verifier grounding and generate–validate–repair loops to avoid silent semantic mistakes [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. We preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory study to answer a well‑bounded question: under a preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired design, does a single‑pass LLM generator produce a lower verifier pass rate than a deterministic template baseline on synthetic intent→configuration tasks? The study was designed to be fully auditable: frozen preregistration, deterministic validator, archived provider call traces, and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes. Our contributions are (1) an artifact‑anchored report of the confirmatory execution and analysis (study id CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...), (2) a reproducible execution bundle with the exact artifacts, provider traces, scoring outputs and hash manifest, and (3) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis of why the confirmatory paired outcome is uninformative about independent generative reliability together with concrete, runnable changes for informative re‑evaluation.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded NetOps evaluation is well established: Batfish and its successors show the value of high‑fidelity configuration validators for pre‑deployment checking and debugging [https://doi.org/10.1145/3603269.3604866]. Recent intent→configuration and LLM→NetOps studies emphasise semantic correctness metrics beyond token‑level scores and motivate generate–validate workflows; representative works include CNSM and network‑configuration LLM efforts that stress intent translation and verifier integration [https://doi.org/10.23919/cnsm62983.2024.10814407, https://doi.org/10.1002/nem.70029]. Our experiment differs by (a) preregistering the confirmatory question and analysis plan, (b) releasing a deterministic validator and full per‑episode traces, and (c) diagnosing a confirmatory degeneracy using immutable artifact evidence rather than proposing new models or unverifiable claims.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand. The preregistered plan (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf3...) specified a paired confirmatory test (H1) where the estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline across N = 120 programmatic tasks (40 per topology class: edge, datacenter, multi‑AS). H1 was to be tested using a paired binary analysis (paired_binary_analysis_v1) with 95% two‑sided alpha = 0.05. Secondary pre‑specified analyses included seed sensitivity (exploratory) and rank‑stability diagnostics. The preregistration and frozen experiment plan are archived and referenced in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json; see hash manifest). Design choices and rationale. Tasks were synthesized from deterministic intent templates producing tight, verifiable required_sequences and workflow policies (example payloads in execution/task_manifest.jsonl). The confirmatory generation semantics for seed_0 were explicitly set to "shared_initial_candidate": a single canonical candidate was produced and supplied to both the baseline and guarded scoring episodes for each pair. This choice preserves exact pairing of candidates and isolates scoring differences if any validator/condition differences exist; it does not measure independent generative variance across conditions. Models, adapter, and validator. Declared LLM: gpt‑5‑mini accessed via adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; configuration archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) implemented full intent constraint checking, transient‑safety rules, and final state equivalence checks; scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation. Execution contract and accounting. Planned_episode_count = 240 (two episodes per pair), maximum_model_calls = 240. Actual completed_episode_count = 240, model_calls_used = 120 (shared_initial canonical candidate per pair). Execution began 2026‑08‑27T14:49:02.808900+00:00 and completed 2026‑08‑27T15:04:49.334056+00:00; the full execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes are archived under execution/*; representative model responses and provider call traces are in execution/responses/ and execution/provider_calls/ (see deterministic_reconciliation.json). Scoring pipeline. Each episode produced a scoring JSON artifact (execution/scoring/task‑NNN‑<condition>.json) containing normalized response, validator_trace, final_state, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after, and a binary score (score ∈ {0,1}). These artifacts constitute the raw data for the confirmatory paired analysis. Contamination and reproducibility safeguards. The preregistration contained a contamination plan: exact‑match flagging and normalized 5‑gram overlap thresholding (≥ 0.95) to detect suspicious exposure; results were archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). All seeds, code, parser versions, validator id/version, and hashes are released. The immutable initial master prompt is preserved at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.discussion: Artifact‑grounded diagnosis. Three artifact‑documented, preregistered factors explain the degenerate paired outcome: (1) confirmatory generation semantics: seed_0 generation_semantics was set to "shared_initial_candidate" and the same canonical candidate was supplied to baseline and guarded episodes for each pair (evidence: execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt; execution/provider_calls/*). (2) templated tasks: programmatic task payloads contain explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) that restrict valid solutions to narrow canonical forms; deterministic template baselines and aligned LLM candidates thus frequently coincide. (3) validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces the same semantic constraints encoded in task templates, increasing the chance a template‑aligned candidate validates. Practical implication: a paired confirmatory test that reuses identical per‑pair candidates cannot measure independent model generative reliability across conditions; it measures whether the validator and scoring pipeline treat identical candidates differently. Recommendations for informative follow‑ups (all runnable from the provided bundle): (A) independent_per_condition confirmatory sampling: remove shared_initial reuse so each condition receives an independently drawn candidate at seed_0; (B) pre‑specified multi‑seed confirmatory design: treat seeds_0..K as confirmatory replicates per condition and adjust paired analysis accordingly; (C) validator diversity: combine deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with reachability/emulation tools or with multiple validators to reduce coupling and measure construct validity; (D) task heterogeneity: introduce paraphrase‑based intent variance and randomized constraint perturbations to avoid deterministic solution collapse; (E) multi‑model comparisons and conditional variance estimation. Reproducibility and audit. We release the full execution and analysis bundle with immutable per‑file SHA‑256 hashes. Key artifact fingerprints: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). These artifacts allow exact reconstitution of the reported run. Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial sampling induced deterministic pairing; prompt sensitivity and seed choices are pre‑specified and archived. Construct validity: deterministic validators enforce template constraints and may not represent operational complexity. External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini), single validator, synthetic tasks restrict generalizability. Conclusion validity: paired design produced a degenerate contingency table; statistical metrics reflect that degeneracy but do not imply LLM sufficiency or parity with templates under independent sampling. Operational implications. For operational evaluators and NetOps tool builders, our artifact‑grounded finding is a cautionary example: confirmatory protocols must ensure independence of generative candidates and validator independence from task synthesis. The provided bundle supports reruns with independent_per_condition semantics and with richer validator stacks to generate informative reliability estimates.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, verifier‑grounded paired experiment and released the full archived execution, scoring, and analysis artifacts. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate confirmatory semantics both the deterministic template baseline and the gpt‑5‑mini guarded condition validated on the 120 synthetic tasks (both 120/120). Artifact evidence (shared_initial responses and scoring JSONs) documents the proximate cause: identical canonical candidates per pair and templated task synthesis coupled to a deterministic validator. The observed perfect agreement therefore does not establish independent LLM reliability in realistic operational distributions. We publish the exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes required to reproduce the run, and we provide concrete, artifact‑grounded modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory design, validator diversity, and task heterogeneity) that are runnable using the released bundle to obtain informative independent comparisons. All archived artifacts—execution/*, analysis/*, deterministic_reconciliation.json, provenance/master_prompt.txt—are available for audit; representative paths and hashes are cited throughout the manuscript.

limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: programmatic templates produced narrow required_sequences and workflow policies; this favours canonical solutions and limits external generalizability to heterogeneous operational intents.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair for seed_0, reducing independence between conditions and causing the degenerate paired outcome.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses (seeds_1..4) were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.

Validator–task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces constraints encoded in the task templates, which can increase pass rates for template‑aligned candidates and reduce construct validity for open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under chosen thresholds, but absence of a flag is not a proof of zero exposure to related artifacts during model pretraining.

Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply only to gpt‑5‑mini under the recorded configuration and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; they do not generalize across model families, agentic pipelines, or other validators.
